scope: 8 sibling opcodes named in BCS-Y-0280's event-family dispatcher table FUN_004D8860
summary: All 8 sibling opcodes dispatch through FUN_004D8860 into the LuaActorImpl vftable, then either bottom out in a 3-byte no-op slot (0x132/0x16C/0x170/0x175) or invoke a receiver wrapper that fires only a Lua callback / maintains non-actor state / performs vtable[9] indirection on a looked-up state object. Zero new chain-key writes; zero new entries to data_dependency_catalog.confirmedIndirectBindings.

siblings.summary: Terminates in a 3-byte no-op virtual at LuaActorImpl slot 49 (FUN_00759DE0). The opcode produces no observable behavior on the LuaActorImpl dispatch path.

Reaches UserDataReceiver via slot 59. Apply (FUN_008A0190) parses a buffer via iterator helpers FUN_0078F810/A60/AB0 then fires _onReceiveDataPacket through FUN_00447260 + FUN_00CC7A90. On parse failure it fires the '[servererror]' message instead. No CharaBase/PlayerBase/NpcBase writes; the wire bytes flow into the Lua callback payload only.

Slot 48 wrapper FUN_00759D20 dispatches into SetEventStatusReceiver::Receive (FUN_0089D860). The receiver apply findings pass (BCS-Y findings JSON, opcode 0x0136 entry) confirmed this path does NOT write actor fields directly: the apply helper FUN_006E67C0 switches on receiver+0x58 to select a lookup helper, then calls vtable[9] on the looked-up state object. No chain-key write at any step.

Slot 60 wrapper FUN_00759ED0 dispatches into SyncMemoryReceiver::Receive (FUN_0089E550). The receiver apply findings pass (opcode 0x0137 entry) confirmed this path maintains a separate sync-memory cache via the registry-update logic in FUN_00775A30 (FUN_00775180 / FUN_007870F0 / FUN_00787ED0 / FUN_00786FA0 / FUN_00780BD0 / FUN_0044D350); no per-actor field writes.

Slot 61 dispatches into SetTargetTimeReceiver - the same receiver class normally bound to 0xD3 SetTargetTime via the central packet dispatcher FUN_004DC690. The event-family dispatcher FUN_004D8860 routes 0x0138 to the same LuaActorImpl slot, so 0x0138 is an alternate-channel SetTargetTime packet rather than a distinct receiver. Apply (FUN_008A04B0) does timer arithmetic on receiver fields +0x04 (uint), +0x08 (uint), +0x0C (ushort mask) compared to FUN_0075BDA0() (wall-clock helper). On significant delta it calls FUN_008A0700 which stack-allocates a Timer object (writing _anon_EE95E5E4::Timer::vftable to a local). Otherwise it calls FUN_008A0370 which fires _onReceiveTimingPacket via FUN_00447260 + FUN_00CC7A90. No CharaBase/PlayerBase/NpcBase writes; timer state lives on the stack and the Lua callback owns delivery to the Lua side.
siblings.aliasNote: 0xD3 and 0x0138 both reach LuaActorImpl::vftable[61] = SetTargetTimeReceiver. 0xD3 routes via the central packet dispatcher (FUN_004DC690 low-opcode fallthrough -> actor->vftable[9]); 0x0138 routes via the event-family dispatcher (FUN_004D8860 case 0x138 -> FUN_005750F0 -> *param_1->vtable[0xF4]).

siblings.summary: Terminates in a 3-byte no-op virtual at LuaActorImpl slot 52 (FUN_00759E10). receiver_opcode_map_inbound.json names a SetEmoteEventCondition receiver class for this opcode via direct_token_match, but the event-family dispatcher path does NOT reach that receiver; it bottoms out in the no-op slot.

Terminates in a 3-byte no-op virtual at LuaActorImpl slot 54 (FUN_00759E30). Same pattern as 0x016C/0x0175: a SetPushEventConditionWithFan receiver is named in the receiver-opcode map by token match, but the event-family dispatcher path bottoms out in the no-op slot.

Terminates in a 3-byte no-op virtual at LuaActorImpl slot 55 (FUN_00759E40). Same pattern as 0x016C/0x0170: a SetPushEventConditionWithTriggerBox receiver is named in the receiver-opcode map by token match, but the event-family dispatcher path bottoms out in the no-op slot.

structuralConclusion: The prior loop's '2-4 new chain-key writes' prediction is structurally falsified for the event-family sibling scope as well as for the original named set. The event-family dispatcher branch does not produce chain-key writes for any of its 28 enumerated opcodes (the 4 originally named, the 8 siblings investigated here, the 0x12F/0x130 KickClientOrder/StartServerOrder handlers already documented as wrapping their own receivers, the multi-opcode fallthrough group, and the remaining handler-bearing cases). The chain-key write pattern from the receiver apply findings pass (CharaBase+0x60, CharaBase+0xDC.+0x10, CharaBase+0xDC.+0x18, CharaBase+0xDC.+0x04[i], CharaBase+0x5D) is specific to a different dispatcher branch (FUN_004DC690's specific-handler cases 0x143/0x144/0x145/0x179/0x17B/0x13D). The chain-key/N-API-reader pairing model is the wrong shape for the event-family branch; its mutations are mediated via Lua-callback dispatch into N-API mutators against global subsystem state (the deferred napi writers pass / WS-H finding).

scanEvidence.purpose: The 8 per-opcode handler functions from FUN_004D8860's switch. All 8 are vtable trampolines that dispatch on (*param_1)->vtable[offset], routing through 8 distinct LuaActorImpl slots.
LuaActorImpl vftable slots ~52..89 to identify wrapper VAs for slots 52/54/55/59/60/61 reached by the dispatcher handlers.
LuaActorImpl vftable slots 0..51 to identify wrapper VAs for slots 48/49 reached by the dispatcher handlers.
UserDataReceiver and SetTargetTimeReceiver wrappers reached by slot 59 / slot 61.
Slot 48 wrapper (SetEventStatusReceiver) plus the 4 slot bodies (49/52/54/55) that are independently confirmed as 3-byte no-op virtuals (`void f() { return; }`).
UserDataReceiver::Apply, SetTargetTimeReceiver::Apply, and the slot 60 SyncMemoryReceiver wrapper - their bodies establish the Lua-only / timer-only / sync-cache-only mutation shapes.
SetTargetTime callees (timer-state stack writes + _onReceiveTimingPacket Lua fire) and UserData callee (data-packet decoder); both confirm no actor writes.

noopSlotConfirmation.claim: LuaActorImpl::vftable slots 49, 52, 54, 55 are confirmed 3-byte no-op virtuals.
noopSlotConfirmation.evidence: Direct Ghidra decomp of FUN_00759DE0/E10/E30/E40: each body is `void f(void) { return; }` at 3 bytes. Matches the noop_virtual_b/e/g/h categorisation in xivl-opcodes/data/lua_actor_impl_slot_lua_bindings.json, here independently verified.

priorMissingSlots.note: lua_actor_impl_slot_lua_bindings.json was missing slots 48 and 60 from its listing (their wrapper VAs were not recorded in any of the four category sections - receiver+lua, receiver-no-lua, direct+lua, direct-no-lua). This recovers them as FUN_00759D20 (slot 48, dispatches into SetEventStatusReceiver - receiver-no-lua category) and FUN_00759ED0 (slot 60, dispatches into SyncMemoryReceiver - receiver-no-lua category).

predictionAccounting.loopPrediction: 2-4 new chain-key writes across the event-family sibling opcodes
predictionAccounting.loopPredictionWindow: The event family sibling findings pass confirms the prediction is false for the event-family branch (0 writes across 12 opcodes investigated to date: 4 named + 8 siblings). No further siblings remain in BCS-Y-0280's enumeration except those in the multi-opcode fallthrough group (which dispatches via actor->vftable[9] in FUN_004DC690, not through the per-opcode handler shape investigated here).
predictionAccounting.rootCauseSummary: Chain-key writes are characteristic of the central packet dispatcher branch (FUN_004DC690's specific-handler cases) where direct CharaBase sub-struct accessors are invoked. The event-family dispatcher (FUN_004D8860) branch's per-opcode handlers route into LuaActorImpl slots that either no-op, fire Lua callbacks, or maintain non-actor state - a structurally different mutation shape that the chain-key/N-API-reader pairing model does not cover by design.
